editorial.description_en: Rice heavy enough to bend the stalk. The most chromatic light colour in the corpus.
editorial.description_ja: 実った稲穂のような、あかるい金色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.766, C 0.108, h 82.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 稲 (ina, rice plant) + 穂 (ho, ear of grain). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Rice Ear" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 稲穂. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — hi-kabe at ΔE00 7.7, kari-ato at ΔE00 8.9, kare-no at ΔE00 10.0. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (262°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
